Russian Strikes Kill Civilians in Ukraine Amid Trump-Putin Diesel Deal

Russian forces conducted strikes in Ukraine, killing at least 11 civilians, including three children, in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia. The attacks targeted residential neighborhoods with guided aerial bombs. The strikes occurred after reports of a diesel deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which Trump defended by stating the U.S. needs oil supplies. Ukraine also reportedly hit a Russian oil hub, with President Zelensky expressing anger over the U.S. diesel deal.
